hook.text: Half the world's coral reefs are dead — biotech offers radical interventions to save the rest before it is too late.

buildup.text: Assisted gene flow transplants heat-tolerant coral genotypes to warming reefs — natural selection accelerated by human hands.

discovery.text: Probiotics for corals — beneficial bacteria protect against bleaching by improving the coral microbiome's stress response.

twist.text: Assisted evolution risks reducing genetic diversity — selecting only for heat tolerance may weaken corals against disease.

climax.text: Cryopreservation banks freeze coral sperm and larvae — genetic insurance for species that may not survive warming oceans.

punchline.text: Freeze it, breed it, seed it — biotech fights to keep coral reefs alive.

quiz.question: What is the risk of assisted evolution for coral reefs?
options: Heat-tolerant corals cannot survive in any ocean temperatures
Selecting only for heat tolerance may reduce genetic diversity and weaken corals against other threats like disease
Assisted evolution creates corals that are toxic to marine life

details.summary: Biotechnology approaches to coral reef restoration include selective breeding for heat tolerance, assisted gene flow between populations, probiotic treatments, and cryopreservation of coral genetic material. These strategies aim to help reefs survive warming oceans.
details.whyItMatters: Coral reefs support 25 percent of marine species and protect coastlines for hundreds of millions of people. Without biotechnological intervention, rising ocean temperatures may destroy most reefs within decades.
takeaways: Selective breeding produces coral lineages more tolerant of warmer water
Probiotic treatments enhance coral resistance to bleaching stress
Cryopreservation banks coral genetics as insurance against extinction

faq.question: How can selective breeding help corals survive climate change?
faq.answer: Corals from naturally warm waters encode heat-tolerance genes. Crossing these with reef-building species from cooler waters produces offspring adapted to higher temperatures.

faq.question: What are coral probiotics and how do they work?
faq.answer: Researchers isolate beneficial bacteria from healthy heat-resistant corals and apply them to stressed corals. These beneficial microbes help corals manage oxidative stress and resist bleaching. Studies show probiotic-treated corals survive thermal stress better than untreated colonies.
